issues.problem: Assumption A2 admits the Windows Job Object mechanism (step 9b, GP9/DECISIONS-r4 I1-17) has no named API and says the fallback 'is to be confirmed or replaced during implementation.' This is an open option left for the coding agent to pick, which breaks the no-TBD rule.
issues.fix: Pick one path now: either name the exact Node 24.15.0 API call for the Job Object, or state plainly 'use the stdin-EOF fallback on Windows' as the final rule, not a placeholder to confirm later.

issues.problem: Line 193 and lines 271-276 use 'could' to describe the deny-pattern match test ('if any pattern in userDeny could syntactically match', 'agentType could not be resolved'). This reads as an open option rather than a fixed rule, even though the logic is otherwise closed.
issues.fix: Restate as a direct rule, e.g. 'if any pattern in userDeny syntactically matches this command (same raw-text containment test as decide.ts step 2b), deny' and 'when agentType does not resolve to any source, case B/C applies (Q23)'.

issues.problem: Line 34 names PiExtension's four hook keys but leaves 'any other key Pi's API requires, e.g. id/name metadata' unspecified, deferring to 'mirror the real @pi/extension-types field names at build time.' An implementing agent cannot write the object literal from this alone.
issues.fix: Either state the full field list for PiExtension now (pull it from the real @pi/extension-types package) or mark this function as blocked-on-dependency and name the exact import path and version the agent must read before writing the object, not 'at build time.'
